customer_question: A design-changed variant (sensor 4) has the same Model Number as existing registered models in the Product List. If we add it as a derivative but the Model Number hasn't changed, the Product List won't visually distinguish pre- and post-change units. Do we still need to add it, and is the existing registration compliant?
question_variants: If our design change doesn't alter the Model Number, and that Model Number is already in the Product List, what should we do?
Can the SIG Product List have the same Model Number listed twice?
How does SIG check compliance - does it check the product's label model number against the Product List?
actual_issue: A new sensor variant (sensor 4) involves a design change from existing registered models but does NOT change the Model Number (same '[ID]' label). The customer asked whether, since it qualifies as a derivative and the same Model Number is already in the Product List, they need to add it again - noting the Product List won't visually distinguish pre- and post-design-change units. The consultant explained: (1) Even if a design change qualifies for derivative treatment, a duplicate Model Number cannot be added to the Product List - the SIG server will reject the entry. (2) However, this is not a problem, because Bluetooth SIG's compliance enforcement works by searching for the product's nameplate Model Number in the certified products database. If the existing Model Number '[ID]' is already in the Product List (which it is), any SIG search will find it - so the product is compliant. The important rule is that the Model Number shown on the product's physical label/nameplate must be findable in the SIG certified products database; having the design-changed variant share the same model number as a registered entry is fine.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth SIG's compliance monitoring works by looking up a product's Model Number (as shown on its physical label or website listing) in the SIG's certified products database. If the model number is found in an active Product List, the product is considered compliant. So if a design-changed variant retains the same Model Number as an already-registered model, that Model Number is already in the database - the product is compliant without any additional action. Attempting to add the same Model Number again to the Product List would be rejected by SIG's server as a duplicate. The key rule: the label/nameplate-visible Model Number must exist and be searchable in the SIG certified products database. Changes that don't alter the model number and don't affect the BLE FW or antenna path don't require any registration action at all.
consultant_answer: Even if it can be treated as a derivative model, if the Model Number is a duplicate, it cannot be added to the Product List again - the server will reject it. When Bluetooth SIG encounters a product in the market or on a website, it checks whether the Model Number is searchable in the SIG certified products registration site; if not found, it sends a warning to the selling company to register. In this case, the product label and website Model Number '[ID]' will definitely be found - so there is no problem. The only situation to avoid is one where the label's Model Number is not in the Product List and would not be found in a search.
decision_logic: When a design change doesn't alter the Model Number and that Model Number is already in the Product List: (1) No additional Product List entry is needed (and attempting one would be rejected as a duplicate). (2) The product is already SIG-compliant because the existing Product List entry makes the model number searchable in SIG's certified products database. Confirm this is acceptable and remind the customer of the core SIG compliance principle: the model number on the physical product's label must be findable in SIG's certified products database.
final_recommendation: If a design change doesn't alter the Model Number and that model number already appears in the Product List, no registration action is needed - the product is already compliant. Inform the customer that duplicate model numbers cannot be added to the Product List and explain that SIG's compliance mechanism works by searching for the label's model number in the certified products database.
risk_if_done_wrong: If the customer incorrectly assumes a design-changed unit with an unchanged Model Number is non-compliant and tries to add a duplicate entry, they will encounter a server rejection and unnecessary confusion. Conversely, the real risk to watch for is a model whose label shows a model number not present in the Product List at all - that would trigger an SIG compliance warning.
